PMACLERN.C 
 
/* Sample program to implement a learn mode in PMAC.  This will generate a motion program 
(PROG 123) which contain a series of X moves which are created each time you press CTRL-B. 
 
*/ 
#include <stdio.h> 
#include <dos.h> 
#include <conio.h> 
#define  SERIAL 555 
#define  PCBUS  123 
#define  COM1  1016 
#define  COM2  760 
int combase,            // base address of the card 
  baudrate,           // baudrate for serial communication 
  speed,              // used for calculating timeout 
  able_to_talk,       // flag for communications established 
  timeout;            // limits how long to look for handshake 
char buf [256];          // holds input string 
int config_card_for (int port,int address) { 
 speed = 9; 
 combase = address; 
 if (port == SERIAL) { 
  baudrate = 12;               // select 38400 baud 
  timeout = 7 * speed * (baudrate + 100); 
  outportb (combase + 3, 131); // set up the PC's serial port for communication 
  outportb (combase, baudrate); 
  outportb (combase + 1, baudrate/256); 
  outportb (combase + 3, 3); 
 } 
 else {          /* PC-Bus will be used for communication */ 
  baudrate = 0;/* when baudrate is set to 0, PC-Bus communication is assumed */ 
  timeout = 7 * speed * 100; 
  outportb (combase + 5,0) ; 
  outportb (combase + 6,0) ; 
 } 
} 
int sendline (char *outchar) {  /* calls send char to send a string of characters to PMAC 
followed by a CR */

 while (outchar [i] != 0) 
  sendchar (outchar [i++]); 
 sendchar (13); 
} 
int sendchar (char outchar) {  // sends a character to the PMAC-PC card 
 int i; 
 i = 0; 
 if (baudrate == 0) {  /* Send data over PC-Bus interface */ 
        /* look for Write Ready bit (bit 1 of base address + 2) */ 
  while (i++ < timeout  &&  !(inportb (combase+2) & 2)) ; 
  if (i < timeout) 
   outportb (combase+7, outchar) ; 
 } 
 else {          /* Send data over RS232 interface (serial) */ 
      /* look for Write Ready bit (bit 6 & 5 of base address + 5 & 6) */ 
  while (i++ < timeout && (inportb (combase+6) & 16) == 0); 
  if (i < timeout) 
   outportb (combase,outchar); 
 } 
 return (0); 
} 
int getline (char *linebuf) { 
 char ic; 
 int i,nc; 
 if (able_to_talk) { 
  ic = nc = i = 0; 
  if (baudrate == 0) {       /* Read data over the PC-Bus interface */ 
   while (i++ < timeout && ic != 13 && nc < 255) 
/* look for Read Ready bit (bit 0 of base address + 2) */ 
    if ((inportb (combase+2) & 1) == 1) { 
/* found it.. read a character and add on to string */ 
     ic = inportb (combase+7) ; 
     linebuf [nc++] = ic ; 
     i = 0 ; 
    }  
  }  
  else {                /* Read data over the RS-232 interface */ 
   outportb (combase+4,2);  // release "hold off" signal 
   while (i++ < timeout && ic != 13 && nc < 255) { 
    if ((inportb (combase+5) & 1) == 1) { 
     ic = inportb (combase); 
     enable (); 
     linebuf [nc++] = ic; 
     i = 0; 

===== PDF PAGE 565 =====
 3A0-602204-363 
PMAC and PMAC2 Software Reference Manual – Change 1, 25 October 1998 6-87 
     disable(); 
     }  
   }  
   outportb (combase+4,0);  // set the "hold off" signal 
   enable (); 
   while ((i += 2) < timeout); 
  }  
  linebuf [nc] = 0; 
  return (nc);        /* Return number of characters received */ 
 } 
 else { 
  linebuf [0] = 0; 
  return (0);         /* No characters received! */ 
 } 
} 
int Cards_On_Line () {      /* verify PMAC is there */ 
 int i,n; 
 able_to_talk = 1; 
 n = i = 0; 
 while (n < 3  && i < 11) { 
  if (baudrate != 0) {       /* serial communications only */ 
   sendchar (24);          /* send ^X */ 
   delay (20); 
   sendchar (26);         /* send ^Z  for serial mode */ 
  }  
  sendline ("RHL:$720") ; 
  i = getline (buf) ; 
  n++ ; 
 } 
 if (i > 11  &&  i < 17) { 
  cprintf ("Found PMAC...\r\n") ; 
  while (getline (buf));    /* clear out PMAC's output buffer */ 
  return (1); 
 } 
 else { 
  sound (1000); delay (250); nosound (); 
  cprintf ("No PMAC found!\r\n") ; 
  able_to_talk = 0; 
  return (0); 
 } 
}

 config_card_for (PCBUS,528);

 Cards_On_Line (); 
 if (able_to_talk) { 
  cprintf ("Now acting as a terminal to PMAC.\r\n"); 
  cprintf ("Press <ESC> to abort.\r\n"); 
  cprintf ("\r\nNow creating program 123.\r\n"); 
  cprintf ("Press CTRL-B to learn current position of motor 1.\r\n"); 
  cprintf ("Press CTRL-D to see learned moves so far.\r\n"); 
  sendline ("OPEN PROG 123 CLEAR CLOSE");

   while (!kbhit()) {     // no key pressed, so check card for data

     sprintf (program_line,"X%ld",position);

     sendline ("CLOSE"); 
     while (getline (buf)); 
     break;

     cprintf ("Learned moves in PROG 123:\r");

     getch (); break; 
    default: 
     sendchar (ic);   // send character to PMAC 
     putch (ic); 
     break; 
   }  
  }  
 } 
 else 
  cprintf ("Can't talk to PMAC!\r\n"); 
}

PMACRAM.C 
 
/*     PMAC interrupt driven program for PMAC using OPTION 2 
Dual Ported RAM.  Make sure a jumper on E83 for IRQ 5 is installed to allow 
PMAC to interrupt the PC at IRQ 5, and a jumper on E65 is installed to allow 
EQU1 to interrupt PMAC's 8259 at IR5. 
*/ 
/* ---------------- PMAC bus port addresses --------------- */ 
#define PMACBUFFERSIZE 1024   /* this our queue buffer size */ 
#define PMAC    528   /* bus address of PMAC */ 
#define PMAC_STATUS  PMAC+2  /* bus status byte */ 
#define PMAC_DATA   PMAC+7  /* transmit/receive data */ 
#define PMAC_PIC00  PMAC+8  /* 8259 interrupt controller */ 
#define PMAC_PIC01  PMAC+9  /* 8259 interrupt controller */ 
#define PMAC_PIC02  PMAC+10  /* 8259 interrupt controller */ 
#define PMAC_RECEIVE  2    /* ready to receive bit */ 
#define PMAC_SEND   1    /* ready to send bit */ 
#define PMAC_IS_SENDING (inp (PMAC_STATUS) & PMAC_SEND) 
/* ------------ PMAC communication interrupt values ----------------*/ 
#define PMAC_IRQ  4   /* 0-7  IRQ0 - IRQ7 */ 
#define PMAC_MASK  (~(1<<PMAC_IRQ)) /* for unmask of PMAC 8259 */ 
#define PMAC_EOI  0x20   /* Pmac end of interrupt */ 
#define PMAC_IPOS  1   /* IR0 for in position */ 
#define PMAC_BREQ  2   /* IR1 for buffer request */ 
#define PMAC_ERROR 4    /* IR2 for general error */ 
#define PMAC_FERROR 8    /* IR3 for following error */ 
#define PMAC_HREQ  16   /* IR4 for communication */ 
#define PMAC_EQU1  32   // IR5 for DP RAM acknowledge 
#define PMAC_NOP  0x40   /* 8259 no operation code */ 
 
/*     -------------- PC interrupt values -------------------     */ 
#define IRQ    5  /* PC interrupt used for PMAC */ 
#define PC_INT   (8+IRQ) 
#define PC_MASK  (~(1<<IRQ))  /* for unmask of PC 8259 */ 
#define PC_PIC01  0x21   /* 8259 interrupt controller XT */ 
#define PC_PIC00  0x20   /* " 0-7 interrupts  "    */ 
#define PC_EOI   0x20   /* end of interrupt */ 
#define ACK   0x06 
#define LF   0x0C 
#define EOL   0x0D 
#define PCBUS   123 
#define TRUE   1 
#define FALSE   0 
#include <stdio.h> 
#include <dos.h> 
#include <conio.h> 
#include <stdlib.h> 
static void  (interrupt far *old_comm_int) (); 
static void  interrupt far pmac_comm ();

void init_pmac_comm () {   /* initialize the PMAC port for interrupt comm. */ 
 
 disable ();                     /* disable interrupts until we're done */ 
 old_comm_int = getvect (PC_INT);/* save original interrupt vector */ 

===== PDF PAGE 568 =====
3A0-602204-363 
  
 PMAC and PMAC2 Software Reference Manual – Change 1, 25 October 1998 6-90
 setvect (PC_INT, pmac_comm);    /* write in our new interrupt vector! */ 
 
/* -------  setup PC's 8259...  -------- */ 
 old_int_stat = inp (PC_PIC01); 
 outp (PC_PIC01,(old_int_stat & PC_MASK)); 
 
/* -------  now setup PMAC's 8259...  -------*/ 
 outp (PMAC, 0);   /* flush PMAC interrupt */ 
 outp (PMAC_PIC00, 0x17);  /* 0x17 = edge, 0x1f = level trigger (ICW1) */ 
 outp (PMAC_PIC01, 0x08);  /* vector for data bus               (ICW2) */ 
 outp (PMAC_PIC01, 0x03);  /* set up for 8086 mode              (ICW4) */ 
 outp (PMAC_PIC01, 0xDF);  /* mask out ferr,err,inpos,breq      (OCW1) */ 
 outp (PMAC, 0x81);  /* DSP enable read */ 
 enable ();                 /* enable interrupts because we're done! */ 
} 
void restore_pmac_comm () { /* restore original interrupt vector */ 
 disable (); 
 setvect (PC_INT, old_comm_int);  /* replace old PC vectors */ 
 outp (PC_PIC01, old_int_stat);  /* restore old status */ 
 outp (PMAC_PIC01, 0xff);        /* turn off PMAC's 8259 */ 
 enable (); 
} 
static void interrupt far pmac_comm (void) {  /* PMAC interrupt service routine */ 
 int  ch; 
 char isr; 
 disable();                          /* don't be interrupted unitl done */ 
 outp(PMAC_PIC02,PMAC_NOP);        /* rising edge of 1st INTA/ pulse */ 
 outp(PMAC_PIC00,PMAC_NOP);        /* trailing edge of 1st INTA/ pulse */ 
 outp(PMAC_PIC02,0x0B);             /* setup to read ISR register */ 
 isr = inp (PMAC_PIC00);            /* read ISR register */ 
 if (isr & PMAC_EQU1)               /* if EQU1 interrupt set, set a flag */ 
  equ1_flag = 1; 
 outp(PMAC_PIC00,PMAC_NOP);        /* trailing adge of 2nd INTA/ pulse */ 
 outp(PC_PIC00, PC_EOI);            /* send end-of-intrpt to PC's 8259 */ 
 enable();                           /* re-enable interrupts! */ 
}

  sendline ("M155->X:$D200,0,1"); /* handshake flag for PMAC to read pos */ 
  getline (buf); 
  sendline ("OPEN PROG 10 CLEAR"); 
  sendline ("TA2");          /* set acceleration time to 2 miliseconds(!) */ 
  sendline ("SPLINE1");      /* set up to do splined moves */ 
  sendline ("X0Y0Z0");       /*     need to have 3 moves (2 done ahead of time) */ 
  sendline ("X0Y0Z0");       /* to do 3rd order spline moves */ 
  sendline ("WHILE(M154=1)");  /* loop until told to stop */ 
  sendline ("IF(M155=1)X(M151)Y(M152)Z(M153)M155=0M113=0M113=1"); 
  sendline ("ENDWHILE");      /* M155 is set to 1 by PC telling PMAC that 
the newly calculated positions can 
now be taken.  M113 set set to 0 
and then to 1 to produce the inter-
rupt pulse which will interrupt the 
PC, telling it to send down new po-
sitions! */ 
  sendline ("CLOSE"); 
  getline (buf); 
  sendline ("M113=0");           /* clear IR5 interrupt input */ 
  sendline ("M151=0");            /* init motor X's position */ 
  sendline ("M152=0");           /* init motor Y's position */ 
  sendline ("M153=0");           /* init motor Z's position */ 
  sendline ("M154=1");           /* let motion program run */ 
  sendline ("M155=1");           /* read first position immediatley */ 
  while (getline (buf)); 
  X = MK_FP (0xD400,0x0804);     /* make these pointer variables point to */ 
  Y = MK_FP (0xD400,0x0808);     /* the proper locations in th DP RAM */ 
  Z = MK_FP (0xD400,0x080C);     /* X,Y, & Z are our position variables */ 
  M155 = MK_FP (0xD400,0x0802); /* out flag to tell PMAC to take the data */ 
  M154 = MK_FP (0xD400,0x0800); /* our flag to stop the program in PMAC */ 
  init_pmac_comm ();             /* setup interrupt vector for our routine */ 
  sendline ("B10 R");             /* and start running it */ 
  while (!done) { 
/*            Now process the interrupt(s) */ 
   if (equ1_flag) {            /* if EQU1 interrupt set, */ 
    equ1_flag = 0;      /* clear the our flag and */ 
  send_command_to_PMAC ();  // download calculated move to PMAC 
   }  
/*   Background tasks can be inserted here!...   */ 
   if (kbhit ())           /* ...like scanning the keyboard... */ 
   if (getch () == 27)  /* pressing ESC aborts program */ 
     done = TRUE; 
  }  
  *M154 = 0;               /* stop motion program */ 
  restore_pmac_comm ();    /* restore original interrupt setup */ 
  sendline ("i8=2");      /* set real time int for every 3rd servo int */ 
 } 
}

Instructions to Change a PROM 
The algorithms (firmware) for standard PMAC's and those with Option 5 are stored in a Programmable Read-Only 
Memory (PROM) IC.  If you need to update to a newer version of the firmware, you can do so in the field by remov-
ing the old PROM chip (the one with the label) from its socket, and replacing it with the new PROM chip. 
On PMAC boards with the new flash memory (Options 4A, 5A, and 5B), the firmware is stored in the flash mem-
ory.  In this case updating to a newer version of the firmware does not involve replacing any chips.  The update is 
accomplished by putting the PMAC board into "bootstrap mode" and loading the new firmware (software) from a 
host computer into the PMAC. 
Backing Up Your Data 
Before you change the PROM or update the firmware, make sure you have any configuration information that you 
wish to keep (I-variable values, M-variable definitions, coordinate-system definitions, programs) stored on disk in 
your host computer.  The PMAC Executive Program has a Save Full Configuration utility for this purpose.  Alterna-
tively, portions of this information can be stored by either selecting the Setup button on this dialog box and choosing 
what information should be saved or by uploading them into the Exuctive Program editor, then saving the editor 
contents to disk. 
Standard and Option 5 PMACs 
In replacing the IC, some static protection is advisable, although chances are low of destroying the ICs.  If you do 
not have a real grounding strap, at least touch some metal with a fingertip to draw off any stored charge before re-
moving the new PROM from its package.  With power off to the card, remove the old PROM and replace it with the 
new PROM, making sure that the notch is on the same end as before. 
Reloading Data 
Now restore power and communications to the card.  If the change in firmware was small, you may be able to pro-
ceed immediately with your work at this point, with all variables and programs retained.   
However, a more major change may result in the loss of your I-variable values and/or your stored programs.  If this 
is the case, you will need to download your old configuration data that you have saved in your host computer.  The 
Restore Full Configuration utility in the Executive program can be used for this purpose, as can the Download Edi-
tor and Download File utilities. 
If you have problems getting going after changing the PROM, you may wish to command the card with a $$$*** 
to reset and reinitialize the card, setting all I-variables to their factory defaults, and empty the buffers.  If you cannot 

===== PDF PAGE 572 =====
3A0-602204-363 
  
 PMAC and PMAC2 Software Reference Manual – Change 1, 25 October 1998 6-2
talk to the card at all after the update, you may want to change the setting of jumper E51 to its non-default state (ON 
for PMAC-PC, -Lite, and -VME; OFF for PMAC-STD) to reinitialize the card when it is powered up. 
Remember to SAVE your I-variable values once you have downloaded them to the PMAC. 
PMACs with Options 4A, 5A, and 5B 
  For any change in the op-
erational firmware, the compiled 
PLCs will have to be re-compiled 
with the LIST LINK file for the 
new firmware version.  It is im-
portant to delete all compiled 
PLCs (DELETE PLCC n) be-

Compiled PLC programs running 
under a firmware version other 
than that which they were com-
piled for can have unpredictable 
consequences. 
If the jumper E51 is ON when a PMAC with the Option CPU executes its reset 
cycle, PMAC enters a special re-initialization mode that permits the 
downloading of new firmware.  In this mode, the PMAC can communicate 
over the serial port only at a baudrate of 38,400, regardless of the setting of the 
baud rate jumpers.  Bus communications is also possible on PMAC's with 
bootstrap version 1.01 and newer (most PMACs have one of these versions).  
To verify the bootstrap version you should type the command VER while 
communicating to PMAC in bootstrap mode. 
In this bootstrap mode, there are very few command options. PMAC will re-
spond to any of the status-bit query commands (?, ??, or ???) with the re-
sponse BOOTSTRAP PROM.  This permits the host to know whether PMAC is 
in this mode or not.  PMAC will respond to the VERSION query command 
with the number of the bootstrap firmware (e.g. 1.01) which will probably be 
different than the operational firmware version. 
To bypass the download operation in this mode, send a <CONTROL-R> character to PMAC.  This puts PMAC in 
the normal operational mode with the existing firmware.  Factory default values for I-variables, conversion table set-
tings, and bus addresses for DPRAM and VME are copied from the firmware section of flash memory into active 
memory.  The saved values of these values are not used, but they are still kept in the user section of flash memory. 
Downloading New Firmware 
To download new operational firmware to the PMAC, send a <CONTROL-O> character to PMAC over the serial 
port.  The bootstrap firmware interprets this as a signal to prepare for downloading of new operational firmware.  All 
subsequent bytes received over the serial port will be considered as binary-coded bytes of machine-code firmware, 
and will be written into the flash memory. 
The host computer should wait at least 5 seconds after the <CONTROL-O> command before starting to download 
the operational firmware.  This delay ensures that the flash memory is ready to be written to.  After downloading, 
the PMAC should be powered down; no other communications should be attempted with PMAC at this time. 
After turning off power to PMAC, the E51 jumper should be removed.  When power is re-applied to PMAC, it 
should operate normally with the new firmware.  The user settings stored in other segments of the flash memory 
with the SAVE command are not affected by the downloading of new firmware (unless the new firmware has a dif-
ferent user memory map). 
The PMAC Executive program V3.x and newer, when it establishes communications with a PMAC in this re-
initialization mode, will automatically notice that PMAC is in this mode.  In this mode, the menu selection "Down-
load binary firmware file.." in the File menu can be selected to take a binary file from disk and copy over the serial 
port to PMAC.  The program then forces you to exit to the operating system.  At this point, you should turn off 
power to PMAC and remove the E51 jumper. 
With older versions of the PMAC Executive program, or with a terminal emulator program running on a PC, the 
procedure for downloading new firmware is as follows (remember to back up your PMAC software and delete any 
compiled PLC programs first): 
9. Establish communications to PMAC over the serial port at 38400 baud.  
Confirm that PMAC is in this re-initialization mode by seeing that it re-
sponds to the ? command with BOOTSTRAP PROM.  If you are in the 
Executive program, make sure that all windows other than the Terminal 
window (such as the position window) are closed, so no other com-
mands are being sent to PMAC. 
10. Type a <CONTROL-O> character in the terminal window and immedi-
ately exit to DOS.  Do not send any other characters to PMAC here. 

===== PDF PAGE 573 =====
 3A0-602204-363 
PMAC and PMAC2 Software Reference Manual – Change 1, 25 October 1998 6-3 
11. Use the binary version (/B) of the DOS COPY command to download 
the file containing the new firmware to PMAC.  The command typed at 
the DOS prompt will look something like 
COPY/B B:V115A.BIN COM1: 
 where B:V115A.BIN is the directory and name of the file containing the operational firmware in bi-
nary machine code format, and COM1: is the serial port being used for communications. 
12. Shut off power to PMAC and remove the E51 jumper. 
13. Restore power to PMAC and resume normal operation with the new 
firmware. 
14. If you want to update your firmware checksum reference value so 
PMAC does not report a firmware checksum error, the easiest method 
is to send the $$$*** command, which causes PMAC to compute the 
new reference value automatically (but it also clears all of your pro-
grams and buffers from active memory).  As an alternative method, 
send the command RHX:$0794 several times.  If you get the same 
value each time, PMAC has stopped its checksum calculations on an 
error, and the reported value is the value it calculated for the firmware 
checksum.  Write this value into reference register X:$07B1.  For ex-
ample, if RHX:$0794 returns 9A3B12 several times, send the com-
mand WX:$07B1,$9A3B12 to PMAC.  Remember that for either 
method, you will need to store this reference value to flash memory 
with the SAVE command. 
15. If you need to re-compile PLC programs, either use the LIS-
TLINK.TXT file that corresponds to the new firmware version, or cre-
ate this file by sending the LIST LINK command to the PMAC with 
the new firmware and storing the response in a text file of this name.

Rotary Buffer Blend On-The-Fly 
If the rotary buffer is executing the last move in the buffer, and a new move is 
entered into the buffer before the start of deceleration of the current move, 
PMAC will blend into the new move without stopping (valid only for  I13>0).  
Abort Command 
When in feed hold mode now causes no movement.   
Power-on/reset position 
When using any type of absolute sensor for servo position feedback, whether 
analog input,  parallel digital input, or MLDT input, Ix10 must be used to es-
tablish the power-on/reset position.  If Ix10 = 0, PMAC will treat the power-
on/reset position as zero.   
Long PLC 0 Programs 
Those that consistently take more than one real-time interrupt period to exe-
cute -- which formerly only intermittently tripped the watchdog timer,  now 
will trip the timer quickly.

the terminal window.  Then select 
the "Load Full PMAC Configura-
tion" option to restore your vari-
ables and programs.  Finally, 
type the SAVE command to copy 
the I-variable values to non-
volatile EAROM, or all settings to 
flash ROM 
User Buffer Space 
8K 48-bit words of user buffer space now reserved for compiled PLCs, reduc-
ing space available for other programs and buffers from 43K words to 35K 
words. 
User-Written Servo 
The memory location of the user-written servo has changed due to the space 
reserved for the compiled PLCs.  The starting address is now P:$B800, not 
P:$9C00.  User-written servos will have to be re-assembled using the com-
mand ORG P:$B800 to replace the existing ORG P:$9C00. 
Ix07, Ix08, Ix09 
Now reported as signed 24-bit values, not unsigned (action has always been as 
signed variable). 
Ix25 
Setting bit 17 to 1 now disables only the hardware overtravel limits, not the 
software overtravel limits (these can be disabled by setting Ix13 and Ix14 to 
0). 
Open Buffers 
Any open buffers automatically closed on power-on/reset. 
Partial Commands 
Any partial commands in the command queue automatically erased on power-on/reset.

Additions 
Flash memory support 
On boards with the new flash memory backup (Options 4A, 5A, and 5B), programs, buffers, and definitions are cop-
ied from flash memory to RAM on power-on/reset.  For these boards, after loading programs, buffers, and/or defini-
tions, the SAVE command must be used to store these in flash memory if it is desired to retain them through power-
down or reset. 
On-line commands 
<CTRL-L> -- Equivalent to CLOSE (quick form of command). 
<CTRL-U> -- Equivalent to OPEN ROTARY (quick form of command). 
DEFINE UBUFFER {size} -- Reserve memory space of specified size for user discretionary use. 
DELETE PLCC{constant} -- Erase specified compiled PLC program. 
DISABLE PLCC... -- Disable specified compiled PLC program(s). 
DISPLAY"{message}" -- This command has been extended to permit {message} to contain characters with 
ASCII values > 127 (non-English characters). 
ENABLE PLCC... -- Enable specified compiled PLC program(s). 
J! -- Adjust command position of addressed motor to nearest integer count. 
LIST LINK -- Causes PMAC to report addresses of internal routines for linking with PLC cross-compiler code. 
Error Reporting 
ERR003 now reported after CLOSE command when an IF statement does not have a matching ENDIF statement, 
or a WHILE statement does not have a matching ENDWHILE statement. 
Motion Program commands 
DISABLE PLCC... -- Disable specified compiled PLC program(s). 
ENABLE PLCC... -- Enable specified compiled PLC program(s). 
IF{condition}{action} -- This single-line condition now permitted in the rotary buffer. 
WHILE{condition}{action} -- This single-line loop now permitted in the rotary buffer. 
PLC Program commands 
DISABLE PLCC... -- Disable specified compiled PLC program(s). 
ENABLE PLCC... -- Enable specified compiled PLC program(s).

I-Variables 
I7 -- In-Position Number of Consecutive Cycles (Minus One). 
I60 -- Auto-converted ACC-36 ADC Address. 
I61 -- Number of Auto-converted ADC Pairs (Minus One). 
Ix10 -- Motor x Absolute Power-On Position Address extended to support power-on read of Yaskawa absolute en-

Ix68 -- Direction-Sensitive Output Bias. 
Conversion Table Entries 
$D0 -- Exponential filter. 
Registers 
Auto-converted ACC-36 ADC Registers -- Y:$0708, X:$0708 to Y:$070F, X:$070F; if enabled with I60 
and I61, these registers in RAM will contain converted analog values from the ACC-36 at the specified address, up-
dated every (I61+1) phase cycles. 
Averaged actual motor velocity registers -- Y:$082A, Y:$08EA, etc. These registers contain the 
actual velocities averaged over the previous 80 real-time interrupt periods (80*[I8+1] servo cycles); good for display 
purposes.  The units are 1/(Ix09*32) counts per servo cycle. 
Dual Ported RAM Functions (Option 2 required) 
1. DPRAM ASCII Communications enhancements: 
2. Permits I3 setting of 0 as well as 2. 
3. Protects against overflow of PMAC's internal rotary program buffer. 
4. Supports command lines up to 200 characters long. 
5. Permits quicker sending of control-character commands.

Update Summary: From V1.15 to V1.16 (July 96) 
Changes 
 In updating from an older 
PROM version to V1.16, it will be 
necessary to re-initialize the 
card, then to reload all variable 
values and definitions, plus pro-
grams and other buffers.  Before 
you change the PROM, you 
should do a backup with the 
"Save Full PMAC Configuration" 
option in the Executive program.  
After powering down, changing 
the PROM, then powering up 
again, re-establish communica-
tions through the Executive pro-
gram.  Issue the $$$*** com-
mand to re-initialize the card by 
typing in the terminal window.  
Then select the "Load Full PMAC 
Configuration" option to restore 
your variables and programs.  
Finally, type the SAVE command 
to copy the I-variable values to 
non-volatile EAROM, or all set-
tings to flash ROM. 
I99 (backlash hysteresis) 
With I99=0 backlash hysteresis is 0 counts, not 4 counts. 
I89 
With I89=0 cutter comp outside corners only add arc if change in directed an-
gle is greater than 90o; formerly 1o. 
I11 
Default changed from 10 to 0. 
I52 
Default changed from 0 to 37137 (1 second slew by default). 
Full Circles 
Full circles executed on any arc command (with IJK center specification) 
smaller than 2-20 part of circle (0.5 arc second); formerly 2-34 part of circle. 
 
Cutter Compensation 
Boundary of cutter compensation lead-in and lead-out moves on inside corners changed slightly; now offset directly 
from uncompensated destination point perpendicular to fully compensated move only. 
 
Additions 
Features 
User-written phase commutation routines (Ix59). 
“Stepper-motor” phasing search method for synchronous motors (Ix80). 
Hall-Effect power-on phase read (Ix81). 
Integrated current (I
2T) limiting protection (Ix57, Ix58). 
Integrated position error limiting protection (Ix63). 
Programmable backlash hysteresis (I99). 
Backlash compensation tables (DEFINE BLCOMP). 
Torque compensation tables (DEFINE TCOMP). 
MACRO ring support enhancements. 
Teach/Learn functionality (LEARN).

Variables 
I55 -- DPRAM Background Variable Buffer Control (V1.15G). 
I62 -- Internal Message Carriage Return Control. 
I89 -- Cutter Comp Outside Angle Break Point. 
I99 -- Backlash Hysteresis. 
Ix02 -- Range extended: bit 19=1 specifies X-register output. 
Ix25 -- Range extended: bit 18=1 specifies MACRO node for flags. 
Ix30 -- Range extended: negative values can be used to invert output polarity. 
Ix57 -- Continuous Current Limit for I2T current fault. 
Ix58 -- Integrated Current Fault Level for I2T current fault. 
Ix59 -- Range extended to 0-3; values of 2&3 enable user-written commutation. 
Ix63 -- Range extended; negative values permit integrated following error fault. 
Ix80 -- Range extended to support “stepper” power-on phasing search. 
Ix81 -- Range extended to support hall-effect phase read. 
Ix83 -- Range extended: bit 19=1 specifies Y-register feedback. 
I1000 -- MACRO node auxiliary register enable. 
I1001 -- MACRO Ring Check Time Period. 
TWS-format M-variables -- Extended to add parity bits in backward-compatible format; bit 6 of global status 
word X:$0003 is set to 1 if the most recent TWS read or write operation resulted in a parity error. 
Conversion table entries 
$2C, $3C, $6C, $7C -- parallel feedback shifted right 3 bits (meant for feedback appearing in high 16 bits); 
supports rollover. 
$18, $58 -- unsigned 16-bit A/D feedback, no rollover of source; to support ACC-28B.

On-line commands 
DEFINE BLCOMP -- Establishes backlash table for addressed motor. 
DEFINE TCOMP -- Establishes torque compensation table for addressed Motor. 
DELETE BLCOMP -- Erases backlash table for addressed motor. 
DELETE TCOMP -- Erases torque compensation table for addressed motor. 
J=* -- Variable jog-to-position; destination in L:$082B, etc. (V1.15E). 
J:* -- Variable incremental jog; distance in L:$082B, etc. (V1.15E). 
J^* -- Variable incremental jog, distance in L:$082B, etc. (V1.15E). 
J=={constant} -- Jog to specified position, make that “pre-jog” position. 
{jog command}^{constant} -- Jog until trigger, final value specifies distance from trigger position to stop. 
LEARN -- Reads present commanded positions for all motors in coordinate system, converts to axis positions, adds 
axis commands to open motion program. 
MFLUSH -- Clears synchronous M-variable stack without executing. 
LIST LDS -- PMAC reports addresses of special compiled PLC ladder-logic routines for cross-compiler (special 
firmware required). 
TYPE -- PMAC reports hardware and software configuration. 
Motion program commands 
{axis}{data}^{data} -- Move-until-trigger for RAPID mode moves. 
SPLINE2 -- Puts program in non-uniform B-spline mode. 
G, M, T, D codes -- Extended to support range of 0-999.99999; formerly 0-99.99999. 
PRELUDE1{command} -- Adds {command} before subsequent move commands. 
PRELUDE0 -- turns off prelude function. 
DPRAM Structures 
Second binary rotary program download buffer added (V1.15G). 
Refinements 
Full circle moves always executed after starting position recalculated due to PMATCH or axis matrix trans-
formation (more tolerance between start and end positions permitted; see Changes, above). 
DISPLAY of I-variables fixed. 
Fast versions of PMAC can interface to ACC-8D Opt 9. 
Fast versions of PMAC can interface to NC control panel and ACC-34C. 
O-commands now saturate at +/-100% of Ix69. 
I52 default set to 37137 for default 1 second stop on ‘\’ program hold command. 
I11 default set to 0 so move sequences start as soon as calculations are finished. 
Ix77, Ix86 reported as signed values. 
RAPID declaration alone on a motion program line no longer causes zero-distance move taking 2*TA time.
